## Body

# Security verdict: #300 at 4ef227f — pass-with-notes

Identity stays a fail-closed boundary. No new unsafe, FFI or dependency (no Cargo change; `parent_of` reuses the existing safe `proc_pidinfo` ProcBSDShortInfo read, which checks `pbsi_pid == pid`, and Linux `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 4 parsed after the last `)`).

## Ancestry (identity.rs 676-722, proc.rs parent_of)
- Every stop refuses: no peer pid, an unread parent (None), parent <= 1 (launchd/init reparent), 64 hops (which also ends self-parents and cycles), and a spawn_blocking join error (`unwrap_or(false)`, both call sites 583 and 945). The old `parent != pid` check is subsumed by the hop limit; the outcome is the same.
- Reparenting can't invent the host: an orphan goes to 1 (refused) or, on Linux, to a subreaper, which is already a real ancestor.
- Pid reuse: the walk is per-hop rather than one snapshot, so in theory a chain pid that exits and is reused between two reads could be read as the new process. The caller can't steer this: on macOS pids are sequential, so the race needs a wrap to that exact pid, inside microseconds, by a fork in the host's tree. The old path had a wider window of the same class (peer pid read by lsof, then a separate ps launch, milliseconds apart). Net exposure is equal or smaller. Not a block.

## Launches
- lsof: `/usr/sbin/lsof` on macOS is a const, absolute, root:wheel 0755. Elsewhere it's PATH-resolved through program::launch, as the bare name was before.
- omp: `program::launch("omp")` resolves on first use from the daemon's own PATH, which the daemon never changes (no `set_var("PATH")`). It keeps only a hit, checks `access(X_OK)` on each launch, and searches again only if the kept path vanishes. Nothing after resolution can redirect it except a change to the user's own PATH dirs, which is the same trust the bare name had. Args are fixed; no shell; `-iTCP@{SocketAddr}` is not caller text.

## Public repo
- The diff has no secrets, tokens, home paths or usernames. No lockfile change.

## macOS proof (CI is Linux only), shared-build at nice 19
- `test -p pij-daemon --lib the_ancestry_walk` ok (real kernel parent_of)
- `test -p pij-daemon --lib register_walk_and_sqlite_roundtrip` ok (local_start agrees with ps lstart)
- `test -p pij-tmux the_walk_keeps` ok; `test -p pij-harnesses parent` ok

## Notes (non-blocking)
- N1 (low, doc): identity.rs's doc comment says the walk "can only lose the host, never invent it". That holds for reparenting but not under pid reuse mid-walk. Reword it on a later touch, or bind each hop by (pid, start) if identity ever needs stronger guarantees.
- N2 (low, sensor scope; perf/reviewer own it): the bare-name sensor matches `Command::new("<literal>")` only, so a bare name passed through a const or variable (e.g. `Command::new(LSOF)` outside launch) is not caught.
